evidence: a-burst-of-new-ssh-connections-is-cut-at-the-limit: baseline 77-79/100-101 send unlisted new SSH through LIMIT_OVERALL, '116' accepts at limit 20/min (iptables default burst 5) and '117' drops the rest; 20 parallel connects from the unlisted peer address (192.168.56.24) after a 61 s refill wait -> 'in 5 / dropped 15' is what those rules produce; the effect file records the connect outcomes seen by the client, i.e. the firewall's verdict

a-whitelisted-host-is-not-limited: baseline 31-34 merges Hiera whitelist with acl, 82-83 accept SSH from each address in rule 100, ordered before the 110 limit jump; the fixture acl holds the peer's +100 address (192.168.56.24+100 = .124, matching whitelist-is-the-hiera-list-plus-the-acl), and 20 parallel connects from it all get in, contrasting with 5 of 20 from the unlisted address; the peer's added address is declared in mutates

purpose covered: Purpose matches the baseline header (DROP INPUT/FORWARD, OUTPUT open, ICMP and SSH in, SSH brute-force mitigation) plus the code's whitelist bypass and purge (line 37). Tested as behaviour from the peer: ICMP and SSH reach, other ports dropped, whitelisted host unlimited, overall limit (burst 5 of 20), per-host connlimit (8 held), per-host recent (14 per 60 s then drop), purge of a hand-added rule by the next agent run, and persistence of the rule set for boot. FORWARD drop and OUTPUT accept are tested as chain policies only: net.ipv4.ip_forward is 0 on the node, so a FORWARD drop is not observable as traffic, and OUTPUT openness is exercised implicitly (replies, agent run). Not covered and not listed under uncovered: the non-default strict mode (strict=true, only listed IPs reach SSH) and the strict_purge=false ignore_patterns variant; these are parameter variants outside the default-fixture purpose, not the class's base job, and loopback rules 001/002 are only covered indirectly through the persisted rule set.
